summary: Proceed as a stage-1b rewrite check (never a submit). The sm_90a build fix is the documented one, and the in-process canary removes the child-process rules problem that held the sibling. The biggest remaining risk is that the kernel is carried over verbatim with its never-executed createpolicy / bulk-copy L2::cache_hint path, the same helper family under suspicion for the swap-AB 715 trap.
justification: Design (kind: rewrite, judged on replaced-kernel rows): sound for H200 at these shapes. FINDINGS puts master's Marlin at 292.5 us (bs=128) and 391.4 us (bs=256), 95% of each shape, against floors of 101.3 / 108.9 us, so about 1.5 / 1.1 TB/s effective. At bs=256, the busiest GPU's 350-450 local routes x 2 GEMMs is tens of us of MMA even at wgmma peak, so an sm80 mma.sync engine plus dequant cannot approach the floor, and wgmma with register-A dequantized weight (swap-AB) is the right tensor-core path. The plan for bytes in flight (>=48 KB of weight per SM, bulk copy plus TMA, 1 producer and 2 consumer warpgroups) is the right order for ~3 TB/s. The register split 40x128 + 232x256 = 64512 fits the launch_bounds(384,1) pool. The archived kernel already bounds its mbarrier waits with a timeout and an error flag, so a protocol bug ends as a flag rather than a 15-minute hang. Expected directions match TASK.md: bs>=128 faster, bs<128 gated off and flat as in-run controls. The M2/M3 targets (<=320 / <=170 us at bs=128, <=497 / <=220 us at bs=256) are physically reachable, well above the floors. The build diagnosis matches REWRITE_READ section 3: cpp_extension appended compute_90, and the fix is TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a with only compute_90a/sm_90a plus the __CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL guard. WEAKEST LINK: no instruction of this kernel has ever executed on the judge, and 'verbatim' keeps createpolicy.fractional.L2::evict_first/evict_normal and the cp.async.bulk ... L2::cache_hint form (patch lines ~160, ~447). The swap-AB sibling died with illegal instruction 715 using that helper family, and a 715 is sticky, so the in-process canary can only name the faulting kernel. It cannot fall back. Dropping the cache-hint operand (plain cp.async.bulk ... complete_tx::bytes) costs little performance at stage 1 and removes the prime suspect. I recommend it even though the spec says ONLY the build fix. Second: the 'binaryVersion/ptxVersion' check cannot tell sm_90 from sm_90a (both report 90). Only the gencode-flag log and the device error flag after the canary actually prove the sm_90a image ran, so the spec should not rely on cudaFuncGetAttributes for that. Third: compile time for 2 families x 4 N buckets of a wgmma template is unmeasured against the 15-minute run and 300 s prepare budget. Log the compile seconds and keep the fallback if it overruns.
confounders: align-parallel-per-expert-verify (current master): the wgmma path bypasses master's _align_parallel_kernel at bs>=128 and runs the expert_map gather + moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 16, 32) instead (2-3 launches). The replaced-kernel accounting must add that align delta, a few us against Marlin's ~300-400 us, so it does not confound a milestone read, but the headline delta at bs=128/256 includes it.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: these set the incumbent Marlin row (block_size_m pick at bs>=128) that the new kernel is judged against. The wgmma path ignores block_size_m (fixed 16-row unit), so it is unaffected; compare against this run's own base Marlin rows from the latest master profile, remembering the +/-20% run-to-run Marlin noise (333.5 vs 316.1 and 403.1 vs 490.2 us between identical-code runs).
post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: no interaction. bs>=128 uses SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum on both paths, and the new w2 epilogue writes cache3 in the layout it expects.
sglang-marlin-path-parity: defines the Marlin bank that stays live for bs<128 and serves as the self-check oracle. The wgmma bank is a second ~0.9 GiB copy; memory pressure only, no timing confound.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite judged on its own replaced-kernel rows (gather + w13 + w2 vs Marlin x2 + act_and_mul) per shape from top_kernels, and bs=1/8/16/32 are gated off as in-run controls. No landed hypothesis acts on the replaced kernels' path at bs>=128 except the align bypass, which is a few us and visible as its own rows in the profile. Reverting or tuning a landed change would not make a stage-1 read more interpretable. The only interpretability condition is in the spec already: a run whose log lacks PATH CHOSEN = wgmma is unmeasured, not neutral. The next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: No rule break found. The self-check, canary, torch.cuda.synchronize and .item() run in prepare/setup (untimed) on synthetic, generator-seeded inputs. kernel_fn branches only on num_tokens and a prepare-time flag; scratch (xs, h_sorted, partials) is overwritten every call, and nothing is derived from data. Weights stay NVFP4 (lossless permutation, round-trip asserted).

load_inline itself spawns nvcc/ninja. Prior CUDA builds on this problem (cuda-dispatch-combine-pdl-verify, flags []) passed the static check, so this is accepted precedent. Do not add any multiprocessing/subprocess call of your own, as the spec already says.
os.environ['TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST'] mutation: environment only, not editing a loaded module. Restore it in a finally block.

Operational, not a rule: a 715 trap is sticky, so the run dies with tests 0/0. Hence the first measurement must be okc check, as specified. Never submit this before a check shows PATH CHOSEN = wgmma with 5/5 tests.
open_questions: Will the implementer drop the createpolicy / .L2::cache_hint operand on cp.async.bulk (the prime 715 suspect shared with the swap-AB sibling), or keep it verbatim and accept that a trap costs this check?

Does the judge's torch version accept '9.0a' in TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST (arch-suffix support in _get_cuda_arch_flags)? If not, the fallback should be passing an empty arch list plus explicit -gencode in extra_cuda_cflags; log the final nvcc command line.
Compile time of 8 wgmma instantiations on the judge: does it fit inside the 15-minute run with prepare's self-check?
Since binaryVersion is 90 for both sm_90 and sm_90a, the image check should key on the device error flag after the canary (set in the #else branch) rather than cudaFuncGetAttributes.
